content:
Last Friday (21st), the ruling in the Hong Kong Alliance case was delivered. In the early hours, police took a woman who was queuing to observe the hearing into a police vehicle. In response to inquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During this time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of having a shirt with some seditious intent," and took her away in a police vehicle. While officers were taking the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and pulled the orange cordon line towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they took down the cordon. A "court-watching volunteer" who was queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) inquired with the police as to why the woman was taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested for suspected "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
